Contributing to qualtdict

Source: .github/CONTRIBUTING.md

This outlines how to propose a change to qualtdict.

Fixing typos

You can fix typos, spelling mistakes, or grammatical errors in the documentation directly using the GitHub web interface, as long as the changes are made in the source file. This generally means you’ll need to edit roxygen2 comments in an .R file, not a .Rd file. You can find the .R file that generates the .Rd by reading the comment in the first line. README.md is generated from README.Rmd, so edit the .Rmd file.

The spelling hook checks documentation against inst/WORDLIST. If it flags a correctly spelled word, such as a package name or a technical term, add the word to inst/WORDLIST.

Bigger changes

If you want to make a bigger change, first file an issue and make sure the maintainer agrees that it is needed. If you have found a bug, file an issue that illustrates the bug with a minimal reprex (this will also help you write a unit test, if needed).

Pull request process

  • Fork the package and clone it onto your computer, for example with usethis::create_from_github("lyh970817/qualtdict", fork = TRUE).

  • Install the development dependencies with devtools::install_dev_deps().

  • Install the pre-commit hooks with pre-commit install. The hooks run formatting, roxygen, lintr, spelling and dependency checks on each commit.

  • Make sure the package passes R CMD check by running devtools::check(). If it doesn’t pass cleanly, ask for help before continuing.

  • Create a Git branch for your pull request (PR), for example with usethis::pr_init("brief-description-of-change").

  • Make your changes, commit them, and create a PR with usethis::pr_push(), following the prompts in your browser. The title of your PR should briefly describe the change. The body of your PR should contain Fixes #issue-number.

  • For user-facing changes, add a bullet to the top of NEWS.md (just below the first header). Follow the style described in https://style.tidyverse.org/news.html.

Code style

  • New code follows the tidyverse style guide. Formatting is done by Air: run air format ., which the pre-commit hooks also run. Don’t reformat code unrelated to your change.

  • Source lines are limited to 80 columns.

  • Documentation uses roxygen2 with Markdown syntax.

  • Unit tests use testthat edition 3. Contributions with test cases included are easier to accept.

Testing without credentials

Tests and documentation examples never use private survey data. The fetch of Qualtrics metadata is isolated in one internal function, and tests replace it with testthat::local_mocked_bindings(), feeding it synthetic Qualtrics-shaped metadata built by the helpers in tests/testthat/helper-*.R. The test suite and R CMD check therefore run without a Qualtrics account.

Only live metadata or response downloads need credentials. Register them with qualtRics::qualtrics_api_credentials().

The maintainer-only smoke check in tools/ replays saved artifacts from real surveys. It is not part of CI.

Repository layout

The vocabulary of the maintainer smoke check is in tools/local-finalize-smoke.md.

tools/ holds maintainer scripts that are not part of the package or of CI, following the unofficial convention described at https://r-pkgs.org/misc.html#sec-misc-tools. The smoke check scripts need Qualtrics credentials; see tools/local-finalize-smoke.md and tools/fetch-local-finalize-smoke.md. tools/autotest.R runs rOpenSci’s autotest as a release gate, with exclusions in tools/autotest-exclusions.yaml; see tools/autotest.md. tools/mutator.R runs the manual mutation-testing release gate; see tools/mutator.md for its scope, saved evidence and required human review.

Before a release

Before a release or a review resubmission, run Rscript tools/autotest.R from the package root; it must exit with status 0. Also run Rscript tools/mutator.R and complete the human review in its saved review.md, following tools/mutator.md. A successful mutation-run exit leaves that gate pending until a maintainer reviews every survivor, fixes consequential gaps or records specific accepted rationales, resolves timeouts and records the final decision. Both gates are local and outside CI.

Code of Conduct

Please note that the qualtdict project is released with a Contributor Code of Conduct. By contributing to this project you agree to abide by its terms.
